## Motivation

Improve native Ascend TP MoE execution across integer and MXFP formats while preserving per-projection precision and shared-expert semantics. Compatible optimizations are selected automatically, without the previous `SGLANG_NPU_TP_MOE_*` experiment flags.

Offline router quantization follows the checkpoint. Online weight conversion is optional through `--online-quantization`; it changes model numerics and requires accuracy validation.

Scope is native TP/EP1. HCCL sizing (#44483) and DeepEP work (#26408) remain separate. Component ownership follows #25663: quant methods select computation, the runner executes W13/activation/W2, and the dispatcher owns routing and finalization.

## Modifications

- Resolve ModelSlim expert/shared schemes through canonical aliases, including integer W4A4/W4A8, MXFP8 and MXFP4. W13 and W2 resolve independently, including mixed floating-point groups.
- Reuse existing shared-expert slots and checkpoint remapping in DeepSeek, GLM and supported Qwen entry points. Validate shared weights and all side tensors before preparation; preserve MoE-TP-local W4A8 compensation, Qwen sigmoid weights, routed scaling and shared addition exactly once.
- Carry immutable typed operands with explicit arithmetic, packing, scales, logical shape, source dtype and stream readiness. Reuse compatible INT8/MXFP8 input across routed and separate shared consumers.
- Select packed routing modes 9/13 only after installed-runtime payload/scale checks match the existing quantizer. MXFP4 passthrough requires a separate probe; INT4 passthrough stays disabled.
- Reuse eligible shared GMM1, activation/quant, TP dual-stream and finalizer `skip1` paths. Guard fused W13 by both projection contracts, activation/clamp/bias semantics and installed device/CANN support. Preserve GELU and distinct integer clamp behavior.
- Unify single-level dense/MoE MXFP4 activation conversion with explicit `rint`, block32/E8M0 and `scale_alg=0`. Weight rounding and the online dual-level format remain unchanged.
- Load offline-quantized GLM/DeepSeek routers through existing ModelSlim linear schemes and resolve Qwen gate descriptors per layer. Preserve correction-bias precision and shared sigmoid gates.
- Add capability-selected fused add/RMSNorm/quant FFN boundaries for compatible GLM/DeepSeek consumers, GLM QKV and both families' dense FFNs. Preserve residual outputs, effective Gemma gamma and source dtype. Floating routers, incompatible consumers/topologies and Qwen3.5 GDN dual consumers retain the existing norm path.
- Add scoped load-time online conversion for floating router, shared, QKV and dense projections: MXFP8 or dynamic INT8; MoE conversion uses the existing MXFP8 method. Offline-quantized weights retain their checkpoint method. Role-specific MoE/shared conversion keeps shared experts separate.

Example: `--online-quantization gate:w8a8_mxfp8`. Targets are `gate`, `moe`, `shared_expert`, `qkv`, `dense` and `all`; explicit targets override `all`. MXFP8 routers request FP32 logits. INT8 routers produce BF16 matmul output followed by an FP32 cast, which is not FP32 accumulation.

Unsupported requested online INT4/FP4 conversions fail at startup. Existing multi-op paths remain the fallback for unsupported fusion. A custom dual-output norm, additional full integer/FP4 fused W13, split shared scheduling and new GMM2+finalize are not enabled. Unsupported ModelSlim dense integer W4A8 shared projections fail explicitly.

## Accuracy Tests

Host validation at `b9bb06c925`: **154 tests and 86 subtests passed** across the focused TP, routing, shared-weight, model-gate, fused norm/quant and stage-boundary suites.

Coverage includes integer packing, TP1/2/4/8/16 compensation, mixed schemes and shared metadata loading, operand/scale rejection, routing probabilities, activation/clamp semantics, MXFP4 rounding ties, fused norm ABI and residual handling, per-layer offline gate selection, online flag parsing and shared fallback.

Pre-commit, Python syntax/diff checks and model import smoke passed. The host uses CPU PyTorch without torch_npu or sgl-kernel-npu; operator boundaries are mocked.

**A5 model/router accuracy, physical layouts, stream scheduling and eager/decode NPUGraph validation remain pending.** Host results do not establish target correctness.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

A5 measurements are pending; no speedup is claimed. Compare identical checkpoints/settings at TP4/TP8 using at least three fresh-server A/B/A blocks, changing one optimization per comparison. Record median/p95 TTFT, decode latency, peak HBM and selected kernels, with accuracy checks.

Local development artifacts provide routing/norm capability probes and benchmark-only ablations. They are not production configuration flags or published target results.

## Checklist

- [x] Replace obsolete TP experiment flags with eligibility checks and existing execution fallbacks
- [x] Format/lint passed
- [x] Focused unit tests registered for CPU CI
- [x] Update Ascend quantization documentation
- [ ] A5 NPU end-to-end accuracy + performance validation

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.

+"""Capability-selected fused add+RMSNorm+quantization for Ascend NPU boundaries.
+
+Wraps the torch_npu fused operators that combine the residual add, RMSNorm and
+the activation quantization MoE/linear consumers ask for:
+
+- ``npu_add_rms_norm_dynamic_mx_quant``   -> MXFP8 (E4M3) / MXFP4 (E2M1) block32
+- ``npu_rms_norm_dynamic_mx_quant``       -> same, without a residual add
+- ``npu_add_rms_norm_dynamic_quant``      -> INT8 / INT4 per-token dynamic
+
+Every path is selected by probing the installed CANN/torch_npu ABI (fail
+closed) and by the complete set of consumer contracts at the boundary. The
+fused operators do NOT return a floating-point normalized tensor: when any
+consumer still needs one, callers keep the existing norm, never ``updated_residual``.
+"""
+
+import logging
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+from functools import lru_cache
+from typing import Optional, Sequence, Tuple
+
+import torch
+
+from sglang.srt.hardware_backend.npu.moe.contracts import (
+    INT4,
+    INT8,
+    MXFP4,
+    MXFP8,
+    ActivationContract,
+    QuantizedOperand,
+)
+from sglang.srt.hardware_backend.npu.moe.tp_fusion import (
+    supports_cann_symbol,
+    supports_npu_op,
+)
+
+logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
+
+# E8M0 scale bytes may be materialized as uint8 or the explicit torch dtype
+# depending on the torch_npu version.
+E8M0 = getattr(torch, "float8_e8m0fnu", torch.uint8)
+
+# --online-quantization grammar: TARGET:SCHEME pairs.
+ONLINE_QUANT_TARGETS = ("gate", "moe", "shared_expert", "qkv", "dense", "all")
+ONLINE_QUANT_SCHEMES = {
+    "w8a8_mxfp8": "W8A8_MXFP8",
+    "w8a8_mxfp": "W8A8_MXFP8",
+    "w4a8_mxfp": "W4A8_MXFP",
+    "w4a4_mxfp4": "W4A4_MXFP4",
+    "w8a8_dynamic": "W8A8_DYNAMIC",
+    "w4a4_dynamic": "W4A4_DYNAMIC",
+}
+
+
+def parse_online_quantization(spec: Optional[str]) -> dict:
+    """Parse 'TARGET:SCHEME[,TARGET:SCHEME...]' into {target: scheme}.
+
+    Raises ValueError on malformed input; 'all' expands to every target.
+    """
+    if not spec:
+        return {}
+    parsed = {}
+    for pair in spec.split(","):
+        pair = pair.strip().lower()
+        if not pair:
+            continue
+        target, sep, scheme = pair.partition(":")
+        target, scheme = target.strip(), scheme.strip()
+        if not sep or target not in ONLINE_QUANT_TARGETS:
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"--online-quantization expects TARGET:SCHEME pairs; got {pair!r}"
+            )
+        if scheme not in ONLINE_QUANT_SCHEMES:
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"--online-quantization scheme {scheme!r} is not one of "
+                f"{sorted(ONLINE_QUANT_SCHEMES)}"
+            )
+        if target in parsed:
+            raise ValueError(f"Duplicate --online-quantization target: {target}")
+        parsed[target] = ONLINE_QUANT_SCHEMES[scheme]
+    if "all" in parsed:
+        scheme = parsed.pop("all")
+        parsed = {
+            **{target: scheme for target in ONLINE_QUANT_TARGETS if target != "all"},
+            **parsed,
+        }
+    return parsed
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class NormQuantizedReadout:
+    """A boundary readout: quantized norm operand plus the updated residual.
+
+    ``normalized_float`` stays ``None`` on the fused paths (the operators do
+    not produce it); consumers needing floating-point input must select a
+    different readout at the boundary, not dequantize ``operand``.
+    """
+
+    operand: QuantizedOperand
+    updated_residual: Optional[torch.Tensor]
+    normalized_float: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None
+
+
+def _float4_x2_dtype():
+    from sglang.srt.hardware_backend.npu.quantization.moe_methods import (
+        _get_float4_e2m1fn_x2_dtype,
+    )
+
+    return _get_float4_e2m1fn_x2_dtype()
+
+
+@lru_cache(maxsize=None)
+def native_norm_op():
+    """Probe the installed MX add+norm+quant ABI once; fail closed."""
+    if not (
+        supports_npu_op(
+            "npu_add_rms_norm_dynamic_mx_quant",
+            ("epsilon", "scale_alg", "round_mode", "dst_type"),
+        )
+        and supports_cann_symbol("aclnnAddRmsNormDynamicMxQuant")
+    ):
+        raise RuntimeError(
+            "npu_add_rms_norm_dynamic_mx_quant is unavailable in this CANN build"
+        )
+    op = torch.ops.npu.npu_add_rms_norm_dynamic_mx_quant
+    if len(op.default._schema.returns) != 4:
+        raise RuntimeError("Unsupported npu_add_rms_norm_dynamic_mx_quant ABI")
+    return op
+
+
+@lru_cache(maxsize=None)
+def native_norm_no_residual_op():
+    if not (
+        supports_npu_op("npu_rms_norm_dynamic_mx_quant", ("epsilon", "dst_type"))
+        and supports_cann_symbol("aclnnRmsNormDynamicMxQuant")

+    INT8,

+    QuantizedOperand,

+    mxfp8_input,

+logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

+# Gate weight formats this module can prepare online. MXFP8 is the first
+# choice (documented native FP32 matmul output on Ascend 950); INT8 matmuls
+# return FP16/BF16 and the FP32 cast afterwards is NOT FP32 accumulation.
+GATE_SCHEME_CONTRACTS = {
+    "W8A8_MXFP8": MXFP8,
+    "W8A8_DYNAMIC": INT8,
+}
+# Declined online gate schemes, with recorded reasons (fail closed):
+GATE_SCHEME_DECLINED = {
+    "W4A8_MXFP": "packed-FP4 gate weights need offline-validated packing ABI",
+    "W4A4_MXFP4": "MXFP4 gate accuracy/packing is not validated",
+    "W4A4_DYNAMIC": "INT4 gate packing ABI and top-k stability unproven",
+}

+        _require_e8m0_dtype,

+def gate_input_contract(gate) -> "ActivationContract | None":
+    """The activation contract the configured gate consumes, if quantized."""

+    if adapter is not None:
+        return adapter.contract
+    if hasattr(gate, "quant_method"):
+        from sglang.srt.hardware_backend.npu.moe.contracts import (
+            linear_input_contract,
+        )
+
+        return linear_input_contract(gate)

+def pair_split_scale(scale: torch.Tensor, rows: int, hidden_size: int):
+    if scale.dtype not in (torch.uint8, _E8M0):
+        raise ValueError(f"Expected E8M0 scale bytes, got {scale.dtype}")
+    if scale.ndim == 2:
+        scale = scale.reshape(scale.shape[0], scale.shape[1] // 2, 2)
+    if tuple(scale.shape) != (rows, hidden_size // 64, 2):
+        raise ValueError("MX gate scale is not token-major paired block32")
+    return scale

+class QuantizedMoEGateMethod(QuantizeMethodBase):
+    """Online conversion of a loaded float MoE router-gate weight.
+
+    Converts once in ``process_weights_after_loading`` (the standard loader
+    hook runs it on fully loaded weights, outside graph capture) and keeps
+    the original float weight so the reference gate remains available for
+    fallback and A/B measurement.
+    """

+    def __init__(self, scheme: str):
+        if scheme not in GATE_SCHEME_CONTRACTS:
+            reason = GATE_SCHEME_DECLINED.get(scheme, f"unknown scheme {scheme}")
+            raise ValueError(f"Online gate quantization declined: {reason}")

+        self.contract = GATE_SCHEME_CONTRACTS[scheme]
+        self.output_dtype = torch.float32 if self.contract == MXFP8 else torch.bfloat16

+    # ReplicatedLinear both create it); online conversion adds buffers only.

+    # loader's sentinel pass (overlap loading) can safely re-run it.
+    def create_weights(self, layer, *args, **kwargs):
+        return None

+            )

+            if q.dtype != torch.int8 or q.shape != weight.shape:
+                raise RuntimeError("Unsupported online gate INT8 quantization output")

+            gate_scale = scale.flatten().contiguous()

+        layer.register_buffer("gate_quant_scale", gate_scale, persistent=False)

+        if bias is not None and self.contract == MXFP8:
+            layer.register_buffer("gate_quant_bias", bias.float(), persistent=False)

+        sample = torch.zeros(
+            (1, weight.shape[1]), dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=weight.device

+        result = self.apply(layer, sample)
+        if not torch.isfinite(result).all().item():
+            raise RuntimeError(
+                f"Online {self.scheme} projection probe returned non-finite output"
+            )

+            "Online %s router gate: %s weights converted after loading "
+            "(original float weight retained; this changes routing numerics)",
+            self.scheme,
+            tuple(weight.shape),
+        )
+
+    def apply(self, layer, hidden_states, bias=None):
+        if not hasattr(layer, "gate_quant_weight"):
+            raise RuntimeError("Online gate weights were not prepared after loading")
+        if isinstance(hidden_states, QuantizedOperand):
+            operand = hidden_states
+            operand.validate(self.contract)
+            operand.record_stream()
+        elif isinstance(hidden_states, tuple):
+            data, scale = hidden_states
+            stream = torch.get_device_module(data.device).current_stream()
+            data.record_stream(stream)
+            scale.record_stream(stream)
+            operand = (data, scale)
+        else:
+            if self.contract == MXFP8:
+                operand = mxfp8_input(hidden_states)
+            else:
+                data, scale = torch.ops.npu.npu_dynamic_quant(hidden_states)
+                operand = (data, scale)
+        if self.contract == MXFP8:
+            q, scale = operand
+            rows, hidden = q.shape
+            logits = torch.ops.npu.npu_quant_matmul(
+                q,
+                layer.gate_quant_weight,
+                layer.gate_quant_scale,
+                pertoken_scale=pair_split_scale(scale, rows, hidden),
+                scale_dtype=_e8m0_dtype(),
+                pertoken_scale_dtype=_e8m0_dtype(),
+                output_dtype=self.output_dtype,

+                else None,
+            )
+        else:

+                q,
+                layer.gate_quant_weight,
+                layer.gate_quant_scale,
+                pertoken_scale=scale.flatten(),
+                bias=bias,
+                output_dtype=self.output_dtype,
+            )
+        if logits.dtype != self.output_dtype:
+            raise RuntimeError(
+                f"Quantized gate matmul returned {logits.dtype}, "
+                f"expected {self.output_dtype}"
+            )

+        # consumes FP32 logits; the cast here is explicit, and for INT8 it is
+        # NOT FP32 accumulation.
+        return logits if isinstance(self, OnlineLinearMethod) else logits.float()

+        h, n = 6144, 1024
+        for packed in (False, True):
+            with self.subTest(packed=packed):
+                k = h // 2 if packed else h
+                original_weight = torch.randint(0, 256, (n, k), dtype=torch.uint8)
+                original_scale = torch.randint(
+                    0, 256, (n, h // 64, 2), dtype=torch.uint8
+                )
+                weight = original_weight.transpose(0, 1)

+

+                self.assertEqual(grouped_scale.shape, (1, h // 64, n, 2))
